Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I love dancing · I hate cooking
FormUseExample
love ❤️+++I love dancing.
like 👍++I like cooking.
hate 👎––I hate running.
negativedon't / doesn't like + -ingI don't like cooking.
📌 like / love / hate + verb -ing
  • 📌 like / love / hate + verb -ing
  • I like reading . · She loves dancing . · We hate running .
  • Spelling: dance → dan cing (drop e) · run → ru nning (double n) · read → read ing .
  • like / love / hate + verb + -ing: I like reading. She loves dancing.
  • Spelling: dance → dancing (drop e); run → running (double); read → reading.
  • Negative: I don't like + -ing: I don't like cooking. (or: I hate cooking.)
  • Question: Do you like + -ing? — Yes, I do / No, I don't.

→ Ordering in a café (I'd like a coffee) comes next.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: dance → dancING → I love dancing. After like/love/hate the verb always takes -ing.
  • ⚠ Люблю танцевать / билегенді ұнатамын = I love dancING — the -ing form, not 'to dance'.

How it works

  • Question: Do you like + -ing? — Yes, I do / No, I don't.

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two lines about your free time: I love … / I hate … .

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

In my free time I love listening to music and taking photos. I like reading, but I hate cooking. Do you like dancing?

Check yourself:

  • Did you use like / love / hate?
  • Is the verb + -ing (dancing, reading)?
  • Can you ask Do you like …-ing?
